name: readable-shell
description: Refuses shortened variable names and short-form options in the shell an agent writes or runs. A legibility guard, not a correctness linter: it checks nothing shellcheck checks, so run both.

RULES.says: which rules hold: `names` for whole-word variable names alone, `options` for long-form options alone

SCOPE.says: what the rules are held against: `files` for shell written into a file, `commands` for the commands an agent runs, `both` for the two. Say that the files are the project's own and outlive the session, and a command is read once if at all

SHELLS.says: which shells' files are held to the rules and have their rules printed, space separated. `detect` takes whichever the project holds. The shells known are `bourne`: sh, bash, zsh, ksh, dash, ash and mksh

ABBREVIATIONS.default: acc arg attr cfg cmd ctx curr desc dir dst enc fp idx len msg num opt pos prev req res src str tmp val var
ABBREVIATIONS.says: the shortened variable names refused, space separated. Setting it replaces the whole list

ABBREVIATIONS_ADDED.says: shortened names refused on top of the list, such as `btn err resp`

ABBREVIATIONS_ALLOWED.says: names taken off the list, such as `ctx` for a Go project or `req res` for an Express one

COMMANDS.default: aws brew curl docker gcloud gh git grep jq kubectl mise node npm npx pip3 python3 rsync sort ssh tar wget
COMMANDS.says: the commands whose short options are refused, space separated. Setting it replaces the whole list. Say that a command is listed only where every option in use has a long form

COMMANDS_ADDED.says: commands held to long options on top of the list, such as `terraform duckdb`

SHORT_OPTIONS_ALLOWED.says: short options that have no long form, each as `command:option`, space separated. Setting it replaces the whole list
